title: Beyond Cultural Knowledge: Evaluating Arabic Cultural Appropriateness of Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.16006v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly serve users whose expectations are shaped by their cultural context, yet most cultural evaluations test what a model knows rather than how it behaves when giving open-ended recommendations, opinions, and guidance. We introduce AraBehave: 1,623 culturally grounded, open-ended Arabic prompts with 29,214 cultural-appropriateness judgments from native speakers across several Arab regions, plus a scoring model whose predictions correlate strongly with human judgments on unseen systems (Pearson r=0.74). Evaluating three Arabic-centric and three frontier LLMs, we find that cultural appropriateness is not a single capability but decomposes into two largely independent components: normative stance and grounded cultural accuracy. translated_title: 超越文化知识：评估大语言模型对阿拉伯文化的适切性
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）日益服务于其期望深受文化背景影响的用户，然而大多数文化评估测试的是模型“知道什么”，而非模型在提供开放式建议、观点和指导时的“行为表现”。我们提出了AraBehave：包含1,623个具有文化根基的开放式阿拉伯语提示，以及来自多个阿拉伯地区母语使用者的29,214条文化适切性判断，并配备一个评分模型，其预测与人类对未见过的系统的判断高度相关（Pearson r=0.74）。通过对三个以阿拉伯语为中心的模型和三个前沿大语言模型的评估，我们发现文化适切性并非单一能力，而是可分解为两个基本独立的组成部分：规范立场和有据可依的文化准确性。表现最佳的通用模型与最佳阿拉伯语中心模型得分几乎相同（5分制中分别为3.84分和3.83分），但二者几乎从不因相同原因失败：通用模型表现出较强的……
tldr: 该论文提出AraBehave数据集（包含1,623个开放式阿拉伯语提示和29,214条来自阿拉伯母语者的文化适切性判断），首次将大语言模型的文化适切性分解为规范立场与文化准确性两个相互独立的维度，并发现最佳通用模型与阿拉伯语专用模型虽然得分相当，但失败原因截然不同。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces AraBehave, a benchmark of 1,623 open-ended Arabic prompts with 29,214 native-speaker cultural-appropriateness judgments, revealing that cultural appropriateness decomposes into two largely independent components—normative stance and grounded cultural accuracy—with the best general-purpose and Arabic-centric models scoring nearly identically yet failing for different reasons.
